EarthPV · Sentinel-2 · TerraMind · TransitionZero · VIIRS · Meta Data for Good

Does our PV map agree with everyone else's proxies?

Three external, independently-produced layers, none derived from this project's own imagery or model, checked against our per-cell PV capacity (est_mwp_rc, the recall-corrected headline metric, ≥400 m² scope). TransitionZero is another rooftop-solar model — a check of whether two independent models place PV in the same places. Night lights (VIIRS) and Relative Wealth Index (Meta) aren't solar products at all — they're proxies for electrification and household wealth, so agreement with them is a plausibility check on where PV should be, not a validation of how much is there.

Background
Sources, units, and what each comparison can and can't show
TransitionZero: units don't match, so this compares rank, not magnitude percent-of-national-total per hexagon+

TransitionZero's file (data/estimated_rooftop_solar_capacity.json, 3,303 H3 resolution-5 hexagons, ≈252 km² each) sums to a value not in comparable absolute units or scope to our MWp figure (confirmed 2026-07-16) — a different methodology and, likely, a different definition of what counts as rooftop solar. Diffing raw magnitudes would be meaningless, so both datasets are normalized to percent of national total per spatial unit before comparing: this asks "do the two models agree on where PV concentrates," which is answerable, rather than "whose number is bigger," which isn't. Rank (Spearman) correlation is the headline statistic for exactly this reason — it's invariant to any monotonic rescaling either side's units might need.

Only - of 3,303 hexagons receive any of our grid cells at all: our own compositing only covers building-populated cells (≈54% of the country's area), so a large share of the "no overlap" hexagons are a coverage gap, not a disagreement — see docs/methods/density.md for the earlier measurement that most of the apparent gap (51.9 of 52.2 percentage points) is cells we have inferred but which score near-zero, not cells we've never looked at.

Night lights: a proxy for "is this place lit and built-up," not for panels themselves VIIRS VNL v2.1, 2023 annual composite, 500 m+

Source: a Zenodo mirror (CC-BY 4.0, no login) of the Earth Observation Group's Visible Infrared Imaging Radiometer Suite (VIIRS) Day/Night Band annual composite, masked and cloud-filtered average radiance, rescaled 0–2000. Nighttime satellite imagery cannot see solar panels (they're unlit); this instead answers whether PV density tracks the same "urban, electrified, built-up" signal that produces light at night — roughly, whether the model is finding PV where people and infrastructure actually are.

Correlation is computed on log(1+radiance) vs log(1+MWp) (both are heavy-tailed: most cells are dark, a few urban cores are extremely bright, and the same shape holds for PV). A large part of this correlation is a shared confound: bigger, more built-up cells are both brighter and hold more roof area to put PV on. Controlling for each cell's total building footprint area (roof_area_m2) via partial correlation drops the coefficient from - to - — still positive and far from zero, so nightlights carry information about PV placement beyond "this cell has more buildings," but a meaningful share of the raw correlation is that shared confound, not new information.

Relative Wealth Index: does PV track affordability, not just urban density Meta / Data for Good, via HDX, ≈2.4 km tiles+

Source: Meta's Relative Wealth Index (Bing tile resolution, machine-learning estimate from satellite imagery, mobile-connectivity, and other covariates — itself imagery- adjacent but not derived from this project's Sentinel-2 pipeline or its PV labels), downloaded from HDX's public, no-login mirror. Values are relative within India+Pakistan (this file's own scope), centered near - for our grid's covered cells, not an absolute wealth measure.

- of - cells have ≥1 RWI tile centroid. Correlation with wealth is real but modest (- raw, - after controlling for building footprint area) — weaker than the nightlights relationship, consistent with wealth being a looser proxy for "can this household afford solar" than "is this an urban, electrified area" is for "is there a roof here at all."

Data & methods what's under the hood+

Our own layer: data/predictions/pakistan/density/grid.geoparquet, est_mwp_rc per 0.1° cell (the currently-published density run). VIIRS: zenodo.org/records/17294744 (Zhao et al., annual VNL v2.1 time series, CC-BY 4.0), 2023 file, zonal-mean radiance per cell via a single windowed raster read (no third-party zonal-stats package needed since cells are regular 0.1° boxes). RWI: HDX Relative Wealth Index, India+Pakistan file, point-in-polygon joined to cells, cell mean over all tile centroids that fall inside it. TransitionZero: as documented above. All three external datasets were fetched fresh for this comparison; none were previously used in this codebase.

Generated by scripts/build_pv_external_comparison.py. Our layer: est_mwp_rc, data/predictions/pakistan/density (current published run). External sources: TransitionZero (data/estimated_rooftop_solar_capacity.json), VIIRS VNL v2.1 2023 (Zenodo 17294744, CC-BY), Meta RWI (HDX, India+Pakistan file).
